filters.name: Compute Geodesic Distance from Border
filters.shortDescription: Compute geodesic distance from mesh borders into vertex quality.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Store in the vertex quality field the geodesic distance from borders. The filter does not bake colors; after it runs MeshLab switches the view to vertex-quality color visualization.

filters.name: Compute Geodesic Distance from Point
filters.shortDescription: Compute geodesic distance from a given point into vertex quality.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Store in the vertex quality field the geodesic distance from a given point on the mesh surface. The filter does not bake colors; after it runs MeshLab switches the view to vertex-quality color visualization.

parameters.label: Starting Point
parameters.help: The point from which geodesic distance is measured. The closest surface vertex is used as seed.

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.help: Cut-off distance. Vertices beyond this threshold are assigned distance 0. Set to 0 to compute everywhere.

filters.name: Create Polyline from Geodesic Path
filters.shortDescription: Create a polyline along mesh edges approximating the shortest path on the surface between two points.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Compute an approximate geodesic path between two points of the current mesh and add it as a new polyline layer. Each point is replaced by its closest mesh vertex; the approximate geodesic distance from the end vertex is propagated over the mesh, as in *Compute Geodesic Distance from Point*, and its shortest-path tree is followed back from the start vertex.

The result is a chain of **mesh edges**, so it zigzags wherever the true geodesic runs across faces, and is longer than the geodesic distance, which the filter reports alongside its length. *Smooth Polyline on Surface* straightens it towards the geodesic while keeping its ends fixed; *Embed Polyline in Surface* then selects it as mesh edges, which it already is.

The two points must lie on the same connected component. The vertex quality of the mesh is left as it was.

parameters.label: Start Point
parameters.help: Where the path starts; its closest mesh vertex is used.

parameters.label: End Point
parameters.help: Where the path ends; its closest mesh vertex is used.

filters.name: Compute Geodesic Distance from Selection (vcglib)
filters.shortDescription: Compute geodesic distance from selected vertices into vertex quality.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Store in the vertex quality field the geodesic distance from the selected points on the mesh surface. The filter does not bake colors; after it runs MeshLab switches the view to vertex-quality color visualization.

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.help: Cut-off distance. Vertices beyond this threshold are assigned distance 0. Set to 0 to compute everywhere.

filters.name: Compute Heat Geodesic Distance from Selection (vcglib)
filters.shortDescription: Approximate geodesic distance via the heat method into vertex quality.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Store in the vertex quality field the approximated geodesic distance, computed via the heat method (Crane et al.), from the selected points on the mesh surface. The filter does not bake colors; after it runs MeshLab switches the view to vertex-quality color visualization. As this implementation does not use intrinsic triangulation it is very sensitive to triangulation. First run takes longer because factorization has to be built.

parameters.label: Euler Step Multiplier
parameters.help: Multiplier applied to the squared average edge length to compute the backward-Euler timestep. Larger values give smoother but less accurate results.
